justifications.durability: The added test is a real guard, and the run proved it by reinstating the regression rather than by observing green: negative-control.log shows the settled-only stage set restored and test_docs_edit_seeds_documentation_when_docs_stage_pending reddening (1 failed, EXIT=1) while the refining-refusal arm stays green, so the seeding assertion fails exactly on the state the change removed. The assertions are independent of their inputs in the sense the rubric requires — node['docs_stage'] == 'drafted' and fake.docs_revisions == ['electron_temperature#rev-0'] are produced by the fixture only after the EDIT_CLAIM_FOR_DOCS_REFINE claim token matches (test_edit_engine.py:749-767), so reverting the admission change leaves docs_stage at 'pending' and the revisions list empty; the two claims are not carried by the test values handed to apply_edit. One deduction: test_edit_engine.py:1597 asserts node['documentation'] == 'seed documentation', comparing the persisted field against the literal the test passed as docs, which reads the write-through rather than an independent source (it still reddens on revert, so it is a guard, not a tautology).
justifications.evidence: The gate the manifest names is the 27-file edit-importing set (the rg -l match) run once at base and once at head, and both results are recorded, not claimed: base.log '412 passed, 10 deselected, EXIT=0' at c98a0d42dc and after.log '414 passed, 10 deselected, EXIT=0' at d5e87ab4a, with baseline_suite/after_suite carrying revision, exit_status and completed true. The declared mutation is recorded in negative-control.log with its EXIT= line and the failing test id. Two deductions: the seeding test drives the docs path only through the FakeGraph surface, so it exercises the parent stage admission and the claim compare-and-set (the marked queries at test_edit_engine.py:295-301 and 743-767) but not the live Cypher the production path issues, which is the fixture's own contract rather than a check of it; and the gate measures the admission but not the claimed absence of a race the comment now asserts, which rests on reading the compare-and-set at edit.py:3525-3536 rather than on a test.
justifications.fit: The landed code follows the file's idiom: the guard stays a literal stage-tuple membership test as it was, the message keeps its 'target docs_stage=...' shape with the admitted set spelled out, the comment is rewritten in the plain prose the surrounding guards use, and the commit is conventional with a body that states the mechanism and carries no AI attribution and no plan or ticket identifier. The added test names (test_docs_edit_seeds_documentation_when_docs_stage_pending, test_docs_edit_refuses_while_docs_stage_refining) name the mechanism and carry no plan label. One deduction: the module docstring at edit.py:59-60 still states the docs-mode precondition as docs_stage in (accepted, exhausted), which the change made false.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The change does exactly what the goal states and no more: edit.py:3473 admits 'pending' alongside 'accepted'/'exhausted'; the claim query // EDIT_CLAIM_FOR_DOCS_REFINE at edit.py:3526-3533 still carries its `WHERE sn.name_stage = 'accepted'` and still sets docs_stage='refining' under a fresh claim_token; the name_stage='accepted' requirement at edit.py:3457 and the superseded/has-successor guard at edit.py:3448 are untouched; the refusal message now names the admitted set (pending/accepted/exhausted); and the inline comment states the rule as the compare-and-set rather than the stage list. The refusal of the stages a docs worker may hold ('drafted', 'refining') is exactly what the unchanged membership test refuses, and test_docs_edit_refuses_while_docs_stage_refining exercises it. The one gap is documentary, not behavioural: the module docstring still names the old stage set.
justifications.reuse: The change adds no definition and forks no capability: it extends the existing stage-membership guard in _apply_docs (edit.py:3473) in place, reusing the pre-existing claim compare-and-set (edit.py:3525) and persist_refined_docs unchanged. Searched by capability for an owner of the docs-stage admission rule — grep for docs_stage membership/equality across imas_codex/ found families.DOCS_STAGE_ACCEPTED (families.py:468, an anchor-selection use), edit._FOLD_DOCS_STAGE_RANK (edit.py:2155, a fold-quality ranking), and the inline-review accept check (edit.py:3786, a different eligibility) — none of which owns the docs-edit admission, so no duplication was introduced and the guard stays the single owner of that decision.
